name: PA-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent running with no polls or expert ratings
model.rationale: Mike Kelly is a well-funded incumbent in an R+11 district, and prediction markets price his reelection around 92%. Justin Wagner's minimal fundraising gives no evidence of a competitive race, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Wagner within single digits, or a surge in his fundraising or outside spending, would move this toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Pennsylvania's 16th District leans firmly Republican, and Mike Kelly has held the seat since 2011. He is running for reelection with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.2 million and holding $1.3 million on hand, while Democrat Justin Wagner has raised under $70,000. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Kelly roughly a 90% chance of winning.

The district's R+11 lean, Kelly's incumbency advantage, and the lopsided money gap all point to a comfortable Republican win. Wagner would need a major shift in the political environment or unexpected resources to make this competitive.
